key_insight: QVal argues that dense supervision signals for long-horizon LLM agents should be judged by how well they predict the quality of intermediate actions, not just by whether they improve final task success. It provides a cheaper way to evaluate these signals without running full downstream training every time.
problem_solved: Outcome-only rewards are too sparse for long-horizon agent tasks, making it hard to tell whether intermediate actions are good or bad. Existing dense supervision methods are also expensive to compare because they are usually evaluated only through downstream performance after full training.
method: Introduce QVal, a proxy evaluation framework for dense supervision signals in long-horizon LLM agents.
Score intermediate-step signals directly to estimate how informative they are for action quality.
Reduce evaluation cost by avoiding repeated full downstream training for every candidate dense supervision method.
impact: This helps researchers and practitioners compare supervision strategies faster and more cheaply, which can speed up iteration on agent training pipelines. Better evaluation of intermediate signals can lead to more reliable long-horizon agents.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing long-horizon agent trajectory with sparse outcome reward vs dense intermediate signals

paper_title: QVal: Cheaply Evaluating Dense Supervision Signals for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
paper_authors: Sergio Hernández-Gutiérrez, Matteo Merler, Ilze Amanda Auzina, Joschka Strüber, Ameya Prabhu
